people.name: Brenda Torres Barreto
people.bio: Leads the San Juan Bay Estuary program in Puerto Rico as executive director. Holds a B.S. in environmental sciences (University of Puerto Rico) and an M.S. in environmental management (Yale). Earlier posts: New York State environmental advisor, head of Puerto Rico's federal affairs office in New York, California Audubon chapter director, and U.S. Forest Service policy analyst.

people.name: Jorge Bauzá Ortega
people.bio: Scientific director at the San Juan Bay Estuary in Puerto Rico, in charge of its water-quality programs. Holds biology, chemical oceanography and marine sciences degrees from UPR Mayagüez; formerly held faculty posts at UPR. Recognized with a 2008 USEPA Environmental Quality Award for mangrove restoration in Condado Lagoon.
people.research_interests: water quality monitoring and data analysis; restoration and rehabilitation of coastal ecosystems (mangroves, artificial reefs); aquatic and ecological sciences

people.name: Ryan Gandy
people.bio: Executive Director of the Sarasota Bay Estuary Program. Trained in wildlife and fisheries science (Ph.D.) and mariculture (M.S.) at Texas A&M; worked roughly 15 years at the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission in research scientist and research administration posts working on monitoring, fisheries advice, citizen science and shellfish restoration.
people.research_interests: fisheries science; research and monitoring programs; shellfish restoration; citizen science

people.name: Nicole Iadevaia
people.bio: Science and Restoration Manager at the Sarasota Bay Estuary Program, directing its restoration projects and science programs. Background includes alpine lake and stream monitoring at the University of Colorado, water-quality and fisheries monitoring at the Florida Fish and Wildlife Research Institute, and project management for Sarasota County and another Florida NEP.
people.research_interests: estuarine restoration; stormwater; seagrass; water quality; science communication

people.name: Heather Moody
people.bio: Operations Manager of the Sarasota Bay Estuary Program, overseeing finances, organizational operations, project management and funder coordination. Earlier career spans environmental education, water conservation with a Georgia utility and the South Florida Water Management District, and nature-preserve management for Palm Beach County.

people.name: Allyson Gardner
people.bio: Executive Director of the Tillamook Estuaries Partnership in Oregon. Holds bachelor's degrees in environmental studies and anthropology from Warren Wilson College, with experience in grant writing, government contracts and nonprofit funding models.

people.name: Claudine Rehn
people.bio: Deputy Director of the Tillamook Estuaries Partnership. Has a business administration degree from Cal Poly San Luis Obispo and a background managing and writing grants for nonprofit organizations.

people.name: Colin Jones
people.bio: Restoration & Monitoring Director at the Tillamook Estuaries Partnership, which he joined in 2021 on its habitat assessment and monitoring team. Earned a chemistry B.A. at Willamette University and an oceanography Ph.D. at the University of Rhode Island, studying marine biogeochemistry and climate records preserved in marine microfossils.
people.research_interests: marine biogeochemistry; paleoclimate records in marine microfossils; estuarine habitat assessment and monitoring

people.name: Flynn DeLany
people.bio: Field & Data Scientist at the Tillamook Estuaries Partnership since 2023, supporting monitoring work. Holds B.S. and M.S. degrees in marine sciences from Stony Brook University, where graduate research examined eelgrass and oyster restoration and their effects on resident communities in Long Island estuaries.
people.research_interests: eelgrass and oyster restoration; estuarine community structure; monitoring

people.name: York Johnson
people.bio: Serves as the partnership's water-quality lead through his position as North Coast Basin Coordinator with the Oregon Department of Environmental Quality. Works on implementing North Coast TMDLs, restoration for water quality, and status-and-trends assessment of coastal pollutants.
people.research_interests: water quality; TMDL implementation and effectiveness; pollutant status and trends

people.name: Robert Pirani
people.bio: Program director of the NY-NJ Harbor & Estuary Program, which the Hudson River Foundation administers; he came to the Foundation in 2014. Before that he headed energy and environment work at Regional Plan Association and directed the Governors Island Alliance. Trained in regional planning (master's, Cornell).
